issue: Is a Rule 60(b) motion that seeks to add a new claim, filed while an appeal from the denial of the initial habeas petition is still pending, a second or successive habeas petition under 28 U.S.C. § 2244(b)?

sides.position: A Rule 60(b) motion filed while an appeal from the denial of an initial habeas petition is pending is a second or successive habeas petition. Under Beaty, it is subject to § 2244(b)'s authorization requirement.
cases: Beaty v. Schriro, 554 F.3d 780, 783 n.1 (9th Cir. 2009)

sides.position: A habeas petition is not second or successive unless an earlier-filed petition has been finally adjudicated. A Rule 60(b) motion filed while the appeal from the initial petition's denial is pending therefore falls outside § 2244(b).
cases: Ching v. United States, 298 F.3d 174, 178 (2d Cir. 2002)
United States v. Santarelli, 929 F.3d 95, 104–05 (3d Cir. 2019)

this_court: The Ninth Circuit follows Beaty and treats the motion as a second or successive petition. The majority affirms on that basis, and Judge W. Fletcher concurs only in the result to register disagreement.
quote: I write separately to register my disagreement with Beaty and to urge the Supreme Court to recognize the circuit split and to adopt the rule stated in Ching v. United States, 298 F.3d 174, 178 (2d Cir. 2002), and United States v. Santarelli, 929 F.3d 95, 104–05 (3d Cir. 2019).
cite: Alexander Balbuena v. William Sullivan, No. 12-16414 (9th Cir. 2020)
